body:
A Rust trait impl's stored name has spaces in it: `crate.<Failure as From<rusqlite::Error>>`. Every command line is split on whitespace (`crate.batch` uses `split_whitespace`), so no command can name one.

In run 9f6696d0464e5adc on task:2414798176c466e4, the agent hit this twice:

- Step 25: quoting the name failed, because the quote marks stayed part of the words.
- Step 27: escaping the spaces with `\` failed the same way.

The `E1001` reply's "Similar names" even suggested the exact names the agent couldn't type. As a result, `Failure`'s two `From` impls could not be viewed or extracted, which D-205 point 2 says must be possible.

### Done when

- `view`, `inspect`, `refs`, `extract` and `delete` all accept a trait impl, and a method inside one (`<Failure as From<std::io::Error>>::from`), in some form an agent can type.
- Every reply that prints a trait impl's name, such as outlines and "Similar names", prints it in that same form.
- `reference.txt` documents the form once.
- A unit test names a trait impl and one of its methods through a batch line.
title: commands: name Rust trait impls
